PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-04-19
42F, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for her yearly wellness visit. She reports feeling reasonably well overall, with good energy on most days. Over recent months family has noticed alternating periods of elevated, high-energy mood with reduced need for sleep and periods of low mood, which she is open to exploring. She works as a retail associate. Sister with schizophrenia. Appetite is good; diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. Sleep varies with her mood. Lives with her spouse and two children. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 120/76, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 165 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.
Psych: cooperative, normal speech rate today, linear thought process, good insight.
Labs (prior week): Hgb 11.6 g/dL, A1c 6.0%, basic metabolic panel within normal limits.

A/P:
1. Concern for bipolar disorder; referred to psychiatry. Provided referral and reviewed warning signs to seek earlier care, including sleep changes and mood escalation.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography discussed and scheduled. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 6 weeks to confirm the psychiatry appointment, sooner as needed.
